title: A steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)-based BCI dataset in children and adolescents
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 47 neurotypical children and adolescents (ages 5-18) collected during a steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)-based brain-computer interface (BCI) session, consisting of a stimulus personalization stage and an online 4-target SSVEP game. Data were recorded with a 16-channel g.tec g.GAMMAsys gel-based EEG system at 256 Hz. The dataset was converted to BIDS format from an original Zenodo XDF release and supports the development of pediatric-specific SSVEP-BCI signal-processing methods.
methods_description: EEG was recorded using a g.tec g.GAMMAsys gel-based system (g.USBamp, g.GAMMAcap) with 16 channels sampled at 256 Hz, earlobe reference, and Fpz ground. Participants completed a two-stage protocol: a stimulus personalization task (12 stimuli varying in contrast and size, flickering at 10 Hz) followed by an online 4-target SSVEP game at 6.25/10/11.11/14.28 Hz across two themed maps, using both personalized and standard high-contrast stimuli. Raw XDF recordings were converted to BrainVision format with BIDS sidecars using mne-bids, following channel order, scaling, and montage conventions from the MOABB Schrag2026Pediatric reader.
